name: Afrika Bambaataa
hook: A Bronx DJ who welded a German art-rock melody to a Japanese drum machine and started electro.
blurb: Bambaataa was famous for playing records nobody expected at block parties, including rock and European electronic music. In 1982 he and producer Arthur Baker built 'Planet Rock' out of a Kraftwerk melody, a Kraftwerk rhythm and a Roland TR-808. It is the busiest crossing on this map, joining German electronic music, Bronx sound systems and a Japanese drum machine in one record. Kraftwerk's publishers were not pleased and it ended in a settlement, which makes it a clear lesson in sampling, borrowing a melody, and who owns one. The track invented electro and pushed the 808 into the centre of Black American music for the next forty years. From April 2016 several men said Bambaataa had sexually abused them when they were boys, the earliest account dating from 1980. He denied it, and in May 2016 he stepped down as head of the Universal Zulu Nation, the hip-hop organisation he had founded, which later apologised to the accusers for how it had responded. In May 2025 a New York court ruled against him by default in a civil case brought under the state's Child Victims Act, after he did not respond or appear. He died of prostate cancer in April 2026. That is part of the record here.
